title: UI Preview: unrelated PR events cancel active preview runs via shared concurrency group
answers: UI preview build canceled by an unrelated PR event
ui-preview label added to another label cancels my preview deployment
why did my preview run get cancelled when I pushed to a PR without the ui-preview label
redundant preview deployments triggered by label changes
body:
Symptom: A UI preview deployment for a PR gets canceled, or redundant previews are deployed, when unrelated pull-request events (for example adding or removing other labels, or events on PRs without the ui-preview label) occur.
Root cause: .github/workflows/ui-preview.yml:concurrency. The group was keyed only on workflow name and PR number (or 'master'), so every PR event shared one group with cancel-in-progress: true. Job-level `if` conditions do not help because workflow-level concurrency is evaluated before job conditions.
Fix pattern: Compute the concurrency group expression so that meaningful events (ui-preview label present, or labeled with ui-preview) share a stable '<pr>-preview' group, while irrelevant events fall back to the unique github.run_id, so they never cancel another run.
Constraints: Any gating that decides whether a run should exist must also be reflected in the concurrency group expression, not only in job `if`. Push events to master use their own 'master-preview' group. Untested end-to-end at merge time per the PR description.
applies: Applies to the UI Preview workflow in .github/workflows/ui-preview.yml; not to other workflows unless they use the same keyed-group pattern.
says: Adding or removing unrelated labels on a pull request canceled my ongoing preview deployment.
Pushing commits to a pull request without the preview tag canceled our active preview.
Stop general pull request activity from prematurely aborting active preview builds.
Changing labels on pull requests is triggering duplicate preview deployments.
Preview deployments should only be canceled by new commits on the same preview.
search: In .github/workflows/ui-preview.yml, the concurrency group must distinguish relevant preview events from unrelated pull request events to prevent unwanted cancellations. Applies to the UI Preview workflow concurrency configuration where cancel-in-progress is enabled. The concurrency expression must map preview events to '<pr>-preview', push events on master to 'master-preview', and irrelevant events to github.run_id. Because workflow concurrency evaluates before job-level if conditions, any run eligibility gating must also be reflected in the concurrency group expression.
